## Question

How many photoelectrons are ejected per second in the experiment represented by the graph of figure?

## Answer choices

- A: A: $6.2 \times 10^{13}$

- B: B: $6.25 \times 10^{13}$

- C: C: $6.3 \times 10^{13}$

- D: D: $6.35 \times 10^{13}$

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image is a graph depicting a relationship between current (I) in microamperes (µA) and voltage (ΔV) in volts (V). The axes are labeled as follows: the vertical axis is labeled "I (µA)" and the horizontal axis is labeled "ΔV (V)".

The graph features a purple line. Here are the details of its behavior:

- For ΔV values less than around -2 V, the current (I) remains at 0 µA, showing a horizontal line along the x-axis.
- As ΔV increases from approximately -2 V to 0 V, the current increases linearly up to 10 µA.
- For ΔV greater than 0 V, the current remains constant at 10 µA, forming another horizontal line.

The graph shows a typical diode-like I-V characteristic. The text "10" is labeled on the vertical axis at 10 µA.
